trust_decision.summary: DiskService#path_for trusts the first segment of a blob key as a tenant name and File.join's raw key segments into an on-disk path, with no segment validation and no containment re-check, so a key containing '..' resolves outside the configured storage root; the decision (accept or raise) is made only in that one method.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names DiskService#path_for by name, and it is the only place in the gem that assembles a filesystem path from a blob key.

fix_sites.entry_point: ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService#path_for (prepended at lib/active_record/tenanted/railtie.rb:125), reached via blob.service.path_for and every Disk download/open/delete/exist? call
fix_sites.module_kind: prepended monkey-patch module on a Rails service class

fix_sites.entry_point: gem dependency floor (activerecord/railties >= 8.1.2.1), which is how the fix protects the non-tenanted 'super' branch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A tenant name only arrives from the app's configured tenant_resolver (default: request subdomain) or an explicit with_tenant call, and TenantSelector requires the tenant database to exist first; a key without '/' is not a tenanted key at all, so traversal there belongs to Rails, and the committed Gemfile.lock already pins Rails main.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keys with no tenant prefix (ActiveStorage::FixtureSet.blob and any pre-existing untenanted blob key) must keep falling through to the stock DiskService#path_for and still resolve under root; a fix that requires every key to start with the current tenant, or that raises on any key without a '/', breaks fixture blobs, and a key must still stay 'tenant/token' after Blob#key generation.

O6_input_shapes: escape via folder_for with no '..' segment ('foo/....secret')
benign tenanted key ('foo/abc123def456') that must keep working

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DiskService#root interpolates the raw current tenant into the configured '%{tenant}' root before path_for runs, so a tenant name containing '..' moves the root out of the tenants directory and path_for's containment check is then computed against that already-escaped root
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: tenant names are resolved by the app's tenant_resolver and TenantSelector only admits tenants whose database already exists (lib/active_record/tenanted/tenant_selector.rb:32-33), so no attacker-controlled traversal name reaches it; the advisory is about blob keys
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 0 files / 0 packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Keys containing no '/' skip the tenanted branch entirely and fall through to the stock Rails DiskService#path_for; the gem itself adds no traversal check on that branch, and the published fix only raises the dependency floor to 8.1.2.1 instead of validating in-gem
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a key without '/' is not a tenanted key, so path handling is Rails' responsibility; the pinned Gemfile.lock already builds against Rails main, where the upstream guard exists
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 0 files / 0 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second path-building method on a storage wrapper (e.g. a tenanted #url/#headers/#delete_prefixed, a MirrorService-style wrapper, or a second DiskService subclass) that rebuilds File.join(root, tenant, folder_for(key), key) instead of calling path_for
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gem already prepends three separate ActiveStorage modules (railtie.rb:120-132) and a maintainer extending the same pattern to another disk-backed service would copy this body; the existing TODO at railtie.rb:121-123 shows this area is actively being extended.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same sprintf(string, tenant: current_tenant) interpolation applied to another configurable string, such as config.active_mailer.default_url_options host or a storage URL base
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: lib/active_record/tenanted/mailer.rb:9 already does exactly this for the mailer host, so reusing the idiom for an avatar/asset or storage host is a natural next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The tenant name interpolated into a filesystem path that is written and reread (schema-cache file path), with no traversal check at that producer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same sprintf/File.join-with-tenant idiom as storage.rb:13/22, already present in the tree, and it goes through a save/reload path the storage check never sees.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22): unsanitised key path components joined into a filesystem path under the disk-service root

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby 3.4.5 (.ruby-version:1), Bundler + Minitest; bin/test-unit and bin/test-integration (.github/workflows/ci.yml:86,109); Rails is pulled from GitHub main (Gemfile:7, Gemfile.lock:1-4), so bundle install needs network
O10_build.project_tests: test/unit/storage_test.rb (DiskService root/path_for, Blob#key) and test/integration/test/active_storage_test.rb (fixture blob, upload, path_for glob)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject keys whose string contains '..' (or run File.expand_path only on the joined path) inside the tenanted branch and leave File.join(root, tenant, folder_for(key), key) otherwise untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but a different property: path_for never binds the key's tenant segment to the current tenant, so with a non-tenanted disk root a key naming another tenant resolves inside that tenant's directory (isolation bug, not traversal); not pursued.

Adjacent, outside this advisory's protection: tenant names are only checked for [/'"] characters by lib/active_record/tenanted/database_adapters/sqlite.rb:37-41, so '..' is accepted and can move the tenanted database file path (base_config.rb:30) outside its directory; that is the database-path sink, not the storage sink, so it is left alone.
unverified: ActiveStorage::InvalidKeyError is assumed to exist in Rails >= 8.1.2.1 (the fix raises it and bumps the floor), but the gem's Rails source is not in this tree; not checked.

Whether the non-tenanted 'super' branch is exploitable at the pinned commit depends on the installed Rails version; the committed Gemfile.lock (Gemfile.lock:1-4) pins Rails main, which is newer than the 8.1.2.1 floor the fix requires, so under the lock it is likely already guarded upstream.

repo_mb was not measured (no shell available); the tree is ~134 .rb files plus one image fixture with no node_modules or vendor directory, so it is estimated well under 5 MB, which is the basis for the tiny_repo flag.
No latest release was supplied for this candidate, so present_in_latest is unknown for every O8 route.
Whether a real application can reach the root interpolation with an attacker-chosen tenant name was not verified beyond reading TenantSelector (tenant_exist? gate) and the tenant_resolver default.
